newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union urges week of protests this month.
newsitem.headline: French union urges week of protests this month.

text.p: One of France's main trade unions called on Monday for a week of protests against the centre-right government from November 12 to 16, but stopped short of urging a repeat of nationwide strikes that crippled France in late 1995.

Demonstrations and work stoppages by members of the Communist-led CGT would particularly hit the defence industry, where the government is planning cuts after the Cold War, the state electricity utility EDF, banks and social services.

"The CGT wants all organisations to come together, entirely or in part, in the mobilisation effort for November 12 to 16," CGT leader Louis Viannet, among the strongest backers of renewed industrial action, told a news conference.

To express discontent with job cuts, press for wage rises and call a halt to privatisation, the CGT called for street protests and work stoppages culminating in a major rally on November 16 in Aurillac, central France.

France's union movement is deeply split over how to follow up a 24-day wave of strikes in November and December 1995 that were largely triggered by a welfare reform plan unveiled by Prime Minister Alain Juppe on November 15, 1995.

France's largest union, the pro-Socialist CFDT, has ruled out staging protests around the first anniversary of the welfare reform, which was aimed at cutting the budget deficit to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
Journalists are due to stage their second one-day strike this month on November 14 to protest against the loss of a tax break.

The CGT's Viannet said the lack of unity among the main unions was "deplorable when blows are raining down, when jobs are being axed, when workers are being crushed...the CGT is determined to do everything to get out of this situation".

Leaders of the militant third largest union, Force Ouvriere (FO), meet on Tuesday to decide their next move in a battle against state budget cuts at a time of record unemployment. FO and the CGT were the main organisers of last year's unrest.
